families.title: Age- and sex-adjusted BMI estimate

applicability.population: Original study: 1,229 participants, 521 male and 708 female. Not individually measured composition.
applicability.errors: Adult SEE 4.1 percentage points; child SEE 4.4. Obesity can be overestimated.
applicability.proposedProductPolicy: Adult mode age 16–83 is an explicit study-bounded product range. Do not call all larger ages biologically invalid. If accepting extrapolation, display it explicitly.

validation: Reject results outside physical 0–100%; do not clamp into apparent validity.
Do not transform this estimate into a personalized weight target or medication dose.

families.title: James and Hume estimates

inputKeys.age: years; used for applicability, not equation

applicability.humeSourceRecommendation: Original paper suggests males over 16 and females over 30; original fitted ages male 40–77 and female 37–80.
applicability.humeSample: 29 men and 27 women, hospital patients; excluded fluid retention and malnutrition. Female regression error around 5.4 kg, male 2.3 kg.
applicability.james: Historical adult estimate; original 1976 report was not inspected. Primary 2022 paper provides exact quadratic coefficients.
applicability.jamesAlgebraicLimit: At fixed height, lean mass peaks at BMI 42.96875 male or 36.14864864864865 female, then decreases. These are derived mathematical turning points, not clinically validated BMI cutoffs.
applicability.proposedPolicy: Return an unavailable comparison with an explanation beyond the James turning point. Enforce Hume source age guidance if age is collected; otherwise prominently state applicability.

validation: Positive finite height/weight. Require 0 < estimatedLeanKg <= bodyWeightKg.
Do not silently clamp or average unrelated estimates.
Use the original full Hume intercepts; some later papers round them to 29.53/43.29.

families.title: Five additional surface-area equations

inputKeys.age: needed for Fujimoto branches and population notes

gehan.population: 401 pooled postnatal historical measurements, including children and adults; 130 aged 20+. Not a universal clinical validation.
gehan.agePolicy: No arbitrary adult-only floor; identify mixed-age historical basis.

boyd.population: Historical pooled formula. Exact universal age/size limits are not established by inspected primary sources.
boyd.agePolicy: Do not invent a validation range. Clearly label historical estimate.
boyd.coefficientNote: Use gram form. 0.03330*Wkg^(0.6157-0.0188log10Wkg)*Hcm^0.3 has a rounded coefficient and is not algebraically exact.

fujimoto.population: 201 Japanese participants from newborn through older ages; general equation corresponds to age 6 and older. Generalization to other populations is uncertain.
fujimoto.agePolicy: General branch age >=6. If younger ages are supported, choose the original age branch explicitly.

takahira.population: Historical Japanese formula; original age/size cohort limits and exact original coefficient not verified.
takahira.agePolicy: Do not invent a universal validation range; identify historical comparison.
takahira.coefficientNote: Use explicitly cited published 0.007241 variant. Other primary comparisons print 0.007246; the 1925 original was not verified. This is a documented variant choice, not a licensing blocker.

schlich.population: 3D-scanned adults, 49 men age 21–68 and 132 women age 20–84. Seven children were excluded from sex-specific fitting.
schlich.agePolicy: Adult-only estimate. Flag age outside sex-specific study range as extrapolation, or make it unavailable under a study-bounded policy. Do not use pediatric age/shape assumptions.
schlich.coefficientNote: Use native meter formulas from primary paper. Common cm constants 0.000579479 and 0.000975482 are rounded conversions.

validation: Finite strictly positive mass and stature; output must remain finite and positive.
Do not round intermediate unit conversions or exponents.
Comparison cards must show method identity; do not average estimates into a diagnostic result.

families.title: Unit choices across solving, splits, projections and conversion

inputTransformations.elapsed: Decimal minutes or a separate HMS control; HH may exceed 23, MM/SS must be 0–59. Never parse a civil Date.
inputTransformations.splitRows: Same selected distance unit for cumulative checkpoints; normalize to meters before segment differences.
inputTransformations.finish: Completed and total use selected shared distanceUnit. If independent units are offered normalize each first.

formulas.outputs: All eight units already accepted as inputs should be available as outputs, with numeric unrounded values plus HH:MM:SS pace.

validation: Unknown unit strings must be rejected.
Only denominators require >0; zero distance/time is valid for a multiplication result. Find-pace with zero elapsed has undefined/infinite speed and must be handled explicitly.
Strictly increasing positive checkpoints and times; no empty/malformed CSV cells.

families.title: Food energy cal, kcal, J and kJ
notes: Use thermochemical calorie: 1 cal=4.184 J exactly.
A dietary Calorie is 1 kcal=1000 cal. Label explicitly to avoid a 1000-fold misunderstanding.
BMR/TDEE already return kJ, so this closes conversion choices only.

families.title: Weight and beverage volume units

inputKeys.beverageRow: count,volume,ABV with global volumeUnit, or validated row volumeUnit

formula.massKg: weight if kg; weight*.45359237 if lb
formula.r: 0.68 male and 0.55 female, explicitly simplified assumptions

notes: Existing beverage-row mode uses kg regardless of global preferences; add a real weight unit control.
US fluid ounce and Imperial fluid ounce differ; never use a single ambiguous oz unit.
US cup means 8 US fluid ounces here; metric cup is 250 mL. Do not equate nutrition-label rounded household measures with exact customary units.

Preserve the timing model stated by each mode: single-beverage mode says hours since drinking began; multiple-beverage mode says hours since assumed absorption and assumes instantaneous absorption. Do not silently merge those meanings.
Fractional counts can represent partial drinks if intentionally supported; otherwise require integers and let amount vary.
BAC% numerically represents grams alcohol per deciliter; do not multiply percent by 100 twice.
Do not determine legal driving limits or sobriety from this estimate.

families.title: 2024 activity references covering all 106 captured choices

formula.aboveRest: Use (MET-1) with the matching baseline. Existing UI floors negative above-rest values at zero; label this convention if any MET<1 is added.

integration: Keep code as a string, preserving leading zeros.
Store basis per preset and branch energy conversion. A wheelchair MET cannot enter the ordinary adult oxygen conversion.
Display activity-specific MET basis, primary code and source; allow code/label search and categories in the selector.
Keep exact MET values; never average the split options or interpolate unmeasured activities.
Retain custom-MET mode for a separately sourced user intensity.
Adult Compendium applies to ages 19–59; older adults and youth have other references. Do not quietly treat this table as age universal.
Every numeric fixture is independently multiplied from official MET facts and the stated model; no product output captured.
families.permission: Official site permits commercial use free of charge, requests citation, and says not to change MET values or combine activities with different MET levels.

fixtures.expectError: Use separate child equation; adult formula is not appropriate.

fixtures.expectUnavailable: Outside original recommended female age over 30.
Beyond mathematical peak; cannot present as a credible rising-weight estimate.
Children excluded from the original sex-specific fitted formulas.
